subject: APAC pool sizing + latency buffer request (Atlas Data commitment)
messages:
From: Oliver Chu <oliver@atlas-data.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@atlas-data.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC capacity ask for committed launch (Q3)

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the call earlier — Atlas is excited to move forward. We have a Q3 launch target and the deal team is working toward a 12-month committed capacity agreement. For initial planning we need a recommended APAC dedicated pool that meets the following: 
- Sustained baseline: ~120 concurrent inference streams at 2k tokens/min average (chat use case).
- Peak bursts: up to 400 concurrent for 10-15 minute spikes (marketing events).
- Target p99 token latency: < 250ms for response tail.
- Data residency: Singapore region preferred, with EU failover.
- Start window: August 1, 2027.

I've attached a simple inputs worksheet with forecasts and traffic patterns (atlas_capacity_inputs.xlsx). Can you confirm feasibility and send a sizing proposal + expected monthly unit cost? Also please call out any latency tradeoffs or buffer capacity you recommend for p99.

Oliver
Director, Platform
Atlas Data

Attachment: atlas_capacity_inputs.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Oliver Chu <oliver@atlas-data.com>
Cc: Priya Menon <priya.m@atlas-data.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC capacity ask for committed launch (Q3)

Hi Oliver / Priya,

Appreciate the inputs — I pulled the sheet into our sizing model and attached an internal draft (chloe_pool_model_v1.xlsx). Early read: feasible with a combination of SG region Dedicated pool + small EU warm standby. Initial sizing assumptions I used:
- Model: Llama-3-Chat-70B compressed (q4_0), ~12 tokens/s inference at p50 on an A100-80GB equivalent kernel.
- Baseline compute: 6 x A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state (handles ~130 concurrent at target throughput with batching).
- Burst buffer: 10 extra GPUs in the SG pool for 20% headroom; recommend autoscaling policy to allow 30% burst for short windows.
- P99 targets: to hit p99 <250ms, we recommend keeping average queue depth under 30ms and enabling KV prefix caching for repeated sessions.

Open questions for Atlas:
1) Are you comfortable with q4 quantization (savings) vs higher-precision variants for long-tail quality?
2) Do you need guaranteed regional-only routing (no cross-border fallback) or is EU failover acceptable under emergency?

I'll loop in Karthik for cost modeling and Marissa for procurement cadence. If those assumptions look OK, we'll produce a formal sizing packet and monthly cost projection.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0192

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: FW: APAC capacity ask — GPU mix & SLO buffers

Looping internal ops/finance: 

Chloe — quick notes on implementation constraints for SG region: 
- Effective supply: Singapore racks currently have higher contention for H100 v2; A100-equivalent throughput estimate is conservative. If Atlas wants stronger p99 guarantees we should propose H100 for burst nodes (lower latency per token for this model).
- Quantization tradeoffs: q4_0 is good for cost but can increase tail latency variance under mixed-batch workloads. Recommend q4_0 for baseline, q8_0 fallback for bursts where quality matters.
- Warm standby: EU warm standby should be kept with minimal cold start capacity (1-2 GPUs) to satisfy residency+DR while not incurring full double-cost.

Marissa — procurement note: Atlas will likely push for a blended committed rate across baseline + burst hours. Can we structure a tranche: baseline guaranteed + pooled bursting credits to be consumed monthly?

Jonas — can you validate the 10-GPU burst buffer assumption against current SG provisioning lead times (need delivery plan by May 10).

— Karthik
Head of Field Ops (inbound)

Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC capacity ask — procurement structure suggestion

Chloe / Karthik — procurement can do a three-tranche commercial structure:
1) Baseline reserved (12-month commitment) — priced at committed rate per GPU-hour.
2) Burst credit pool — pre-purchased monthly credits with discounted overage pricing; unused credits roll monthly up to 30%.
3) Failover standby — small monthly fee for EU warm standby (kept at minimal capacity).

I'll draft language gloss for the SOW and propose margin and discount bands in the attached doc. If Atlas agrees to a baseline commit (6 GPUs) + 10 burst credits, we can hold SG capacity if signed by May 20.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Oliver / Priya — thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps below: 

Summary proposal (high level):
- Baseline SG Dedicated pool: 6 A100-equivalent GPUs (handles steady 120 concurrent streams).
- Burst buffer: 10 GPUs (H100-preferred for p99-sensitive bursts) available via autoscale; 30% headroom allowed for short windows.
- Warm EU standby: 2 GPUs for residency/DR.
- Quantization policy: q4_0 baseline, q8_0 fallback for quality-sensitive bursts.
- Estimated monthly committed cost (baseline + standby): $XX,XXX/mo (detailed cost workbook attached). Burst credits priced separately per-hour; suggested tranche discounts included.
- SLA/latency mitigation: we will enable prefix caching and a KV hot-path for session reuse; expected p99 < 250ms under proposed layout.

Requested actions: 
1) Please confirm acceptance of the baseline + burst tranche structure (reply with CONFIRM).
2) If accepted, sign the attached SOW (we can iterate language) and we will submit capacity hold request to infra by May 20.
3) Let us know if strict regional-only routing is required — EU failover is currently configured as emergency-only.

Attachments: pool_sizing_model_v2.xlsx, SLA-buffering-summary.pdf
